stages.title: Numerical optimization: research guide
stages.html:
Numerical optimization

Scale, initialize, constrain, and verify nonlinear estimators.

A credible optimum survives alternative starting values and has a small gradient, admissible parameters, and sensible curvature.

Workflow. Scale parameters, use defensible starts, and verify more than one convergence signal.

Diagnostic: Inspect gradient, Hessian, bounds, and sensitivity to starts. The main failure to avoid is a local or boundary solution reported as a unique optimum.

stages.title: Numerical optimization intuition lab
stages.note: The mixture negative log-likelihood is symmetric with two minima; slide the optimizer's start across the local maximum at 0 and watch it converge to a different solution.
stages.template:
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.optimize import minimize
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
sep = {{sep}}; x0 = {{x0}}
z = rng.random(300) < 0.5
data = np.where(z, rng.normal(sep, 1, 300), rng.normal(-sep, 1, 300))
def nll(mu):
    m = np.atleast_1d(mu)[0]
    dens = 0.5*np.exp(-0.5*(data - m)**2) + 0.5*np.exp(-0.5*(data + m)**2)
    return -np.sum(np.log(dens + 1e-12))
grid = np.linspace(-sep - 3, sep + 3, 400)
curve = np.array([nll(m) for m in grid])
opt = minimize(nll, x0, method="Nelder-Mead")
mstar = opt.x[0]
grad = (nll(mstar + 1e-4) - nll(mstar - 1e-4)) / 2e-4
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 3.7))
plt.plot(grid, curve, color="#d1495b", lw=2)
plt.axvline(x0, color="#8a8a8a", ls=":", lw=1.5, label=f"start = {x0:.1f}")
plt.axvline(mstar, color="#3a7d44", ls="--", lw=1.5, label=f"converged μ = {mstar:.2f}")
plt.xlabel("μ"); plt.ylabel("negative log-likelihood")
plt.title("Multimodal objective: the start decides the basin"); plt.legend()
print(f"start = {x0:.2f}  ->  converged mu = {mstar:.3f}")
print(f"gradient at solution = {grad:.2e}  (small => a local optimum, not necessarily unique)")

stages.title: Numerical optimization: worked Python model
stages.note: Run the reproducible example, then change one assumption and compare the output.
stages.code:
import numpy as np
y = np.array([1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 1, 1])
grid = np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 181)
loglike = np.array([(y*np.log(p) + (1-y)*np.log(1-p)).sum() for p in grid])
p_hat = grid[np.argmax(loglike)]
print(f"Grid MLE: {p_hat:.3f}")
print(f"Sample mean: {y.mean():.3f}")
